books.title: O Pioneers!
books.author: Willa Cather
books.desc: When her father dies, young Alexandra Bergson takes charge of the family farm on the harsh Nebraska prairie and believes in the land when others give up.
about: On the windswept prairie near the little town of Hanover, Nebraska, the Swedish immigrant John Bergson dies after years of struggle with the land, leaving his farm to the care of his capable eldest daughter, Alexandra. While her brothers and many neighbours lose heart and want to sell, Alexandra has faith in the soil and in the future. Her friendship with Carl Linstrum, a gentle neighbour who leaves for the city, and her love for her youngest brother Emil shape the years that follow.

Cather celebrates the courage and vision of the immigrant settlers of the Great Plains and the beauty of the prairie through the seasons. Alongside Alexandra's story runs a story of passion between Emil and a married neighbour, Marie Shabata, showing the price of desire in a close-knit farming community.

O Pioneers! was published in 1913 and is often seen as Willa Cather's first great novel. It is the first of her three novels of the Great Plains, sometimes called her Prairie Trilogy, together with The Song of the Lark and My Ántonia.

books.title: Sister Carrie
books.author: Theodore Dreiser
books.desc: A small-town girl arrives in Chicago with almost nothing and climbs towards fame, while the man who loves her slowly falls, in a landmark of American realism.
about: In 1889, eighteen-year-old Caroline Meeber, known to her family as Sister Carrie, leaves her small Wisconsin town for Chicago with a few dollars and great hopes. Factory work is hard and poorly paid, and she soon accepts the help and attentions of Charles Drouet, a cheerful travelling salesman. Through him she meets George Hurstwood, the prosperous and respected manager of a fashionable saloon, and her life, and his, take unexpected turns that lead them to New York.

Dreiser describes the lure of the big city, money and fine things with great detail and without moral judgement, showing characters driven by desire, chance and circumstance. As Carrie rises, the novel follows another life heading the opposite way, in one of the most powerful portraits of decline in American fiction.

Sister Carrie was Dreiser's first novel, published by Doubleday, Page and Company on 8 November 1900. The publisher, uneasy about a heroine who lives outside marriage without being punished, printed only a small edition and did little to promote it. It is now regarded as a founding work of American naturalism.
books.author_short: American novelist and journalist (1871–1945), author of Sister Carrie and An American Tragedy.
author_long: Theodore Dreiser was born in Terre Haute, Indiana, on 27 August 1871, into a large and poor family. He worked for about ten years as a journalist, writing about life in fast-growing cities such as Chicago and New York, before turning to fiction. He died in Hollywood, California, on 28 December 1945.

Dreiser was the leading American writer of the naturalist school, showing how money, environment and social pressures shape people's lives. His best-known novels are Sister Carrie (1900) and An American Tragedy (1925).

books.title: Typee
books.author: Herman Melville
books.desc: Two sailors desert their whaling ship in the Marquesas Islands and find themselves guests, or perhaps prisoners, of the feared Typee people in a hidden valley.
about: Tired of hard life and harsh treatment aboard a whaling ship, the young sailor known as Tom and his friend Toby jump ship at the island of Nukuheva in the Marquesas. Struggling across the mountains, they descend into the valley of the Typee, a people the sailors fear as cannibals. Instead they are welcomed, fed and cared for, and Tom, nursing an injured leg, lives among them, befriending the devoted Kory-Kory and the lovely Fayaway, while wondering whether he will ever be allowed to leave.

Melville mixes adventure, travel description and reflection, often comparing the life of the islanders favourably with that of so-called civilised Western society and criticising missionaries and colonial powers. At the same time the book views the Polynesian people through the exotic and stereotyped lens of nineteenth-century travel writing.

Typee, Melville's first book, was published in 1846 by John Murray in London and Wiley and Putnam in New York. It draws, with much invention, on his own experience of deserting the whaler Acushnet at Nuku Hiva in 1842 with a shipmate, Richard Tobias Greene. It was a sensational success and made Melville famous as the man who had lived among cannibals.

books.title: Ben-Hur
books.author: Lew Wallace
books.desc: Falsely accused by a boyhood friend, the Jewish prince Judah Ben-Hur is sent to the Roman galleys, and his quest for justice crosses the life of Christ.
about: Judah Ben-Hur, a young Jewish nobleman of Jerusalem, is reunited with his childhood friend Messala, now an arrogant Roman officer. When a tile falls from Ben-Hur's roof onto the new Roman governor, Messala seizes the chance to ruin him: Judah is condemned to the galleys and his mother and sister disappear. Years later, after saving the life of the Roman commander Quintus Arrius, Judah returns to the East determined to find his family and confront Messala.

Wallace combines a grand adventure, with sea battles and the famous chariot race in Antioch, with the story of the coming of Christ, whose life crosses Judah's at key moments. The novel draws a broad picture of the Roman world and Judea and explores revenge, faith and forgiveness.

Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ was published by Harper and Brothers on 12 November 1880. It became the best-selling American novel of the nineteenth century, overtaking Uncle Tom's Cabin, and has been adapted for the stage and the screen, including a 1925 film.
books.author_short: American soldier, statesman and novelist (1827–1905), author of Ben-Hur.
author_long: Lew Wallace was born on 10 April 1827 in Brookville, Indiana. He served in the Mexican War and in the American Civil War, in which he rose to the rank of major general. He was later governor of the New Mexico Territory from 1878 to 1881 and United States minister to the Ottoman Empire from 1881 to 1885. He died in Crawfordsville, Indiana, on 15 February 1905.

Wallace wrote Ben-Hur (1880) while governor of New Mexico. Its enormous success made it one of the most influential Christian books of the nineteenth century, and it remains by far his best-known work.

books.title: Pollyanna
books.author: Eleanor H. Porter
books.desc: An orphaned girl comes to live with her stern aunt in a small Vermont town and wins over everyone with her "glad game": always finding something to be glad about.
about: After the death of her father, a poor missionary minister, eleven-year-old Pollyanna Whittier is sent to live with her wealthy and severe Aunt Polly in the town of Beldingsville. Aunt Polly takes her in out of duty, not love, and gives her a bare attic room. But Pollyanna has a secret her father taught her: the glad game, in which she looks for something to be glad about in every situation, however bad.

Pollyanna's cheerfulness gradually touches the lonely, the sick and the bitter around her, from the reclusive Mr Pendleton to a bedridden invalid and an orphan boy named Jimmy. The story is a gentle and warm-hearted tale about optimism, kindness and the power of seeing the good in life.

Pollyanna was published in 1913 and became a great success and a classic of children's literature. Porter wrote one sequel, Pollyanna Grows Up (1915); many later sequels were written by other authors.
author_long: Eleanor Emily Hodgman Porter was born on 19 December 1868 in Littleton, New Hampshire. She published stories in magazines and a number of novels for adults and young readers. She died on 21 May 1920.
Her best-known book by far is Pollyanna (1913), a classic of children's literature, followed by its sequel Pollyanna Grows Up (1915).
